source.description: User-supplied 210.716625-second abstract offset-print music video. Original lyrics, title, branding and footage are excluded from reusable entries and previews.
source.reuse_policy: Original code-drawn studies and neutral copy; no source artwork or audio reused.

analysis_provenance.sampling: 106 chronological overview frames and 31 scene-cut frames; final bounded design reviewed 50–52.375 s at nominal 8 fps and 72–73.9 s at nominal 10 fps. No continuous playback or audio analysis.
limitations: Whole-video coverage is from about 2 s overview samples plus 31 detected cuts; only two dense windows (50 to 52.375 s at 8 fps, 72 to 73.9 s at 10 fps) are used here.
No audio was analysed; no tempo, beat or vocal-sync claim is made.
Colours are approximate readings from compressed contact sheets.
All timings in the templates are authored defaults chosen to resemble sampled behaviour, not measured source values.
Source lyrics, title, credits, subtitles and the signature mark are excluded from all reusable text.

dense_findings.observation: Chorus stacked block on maroon/black rays. The active vermilion box steps word to word at intervals of roughly 0.25 to 0.5 s. At several hand-overs two adjacent tokens are filled in the same sample (about 50.375, 51.5, 51.875, 52.375), so the relay has a short overlap rather than strictly one lit token. Completed words are bright off-white; upcoming words are dim grey. Between 50.875 and 51.125 the completed block shrinks and moves to the top-right as a history block (51.0 shows it mid-move with a faint ghost at the old position), while the next stanza appears dim at top-left. The history block keeps its last active fill at 51.125 to 51.25 and is neutral by 51.625. The ink silhouette at the vanishing point changes outline almost every sample (lobed, spiky, gear-like) and has a ring of light dots.
dense_findings.uncertainty: 8 fps sampling: the overlap length could be anything up to about 0.125 s; the fill could pop or wipe within one frame interval. The shrink-and-move appears continuous but its easing cannot be measured. Silhouette change may be a morph or per-frame replacement.

dense_findings.observation: At 72.0 to 72.1 a black spiky burst with cream and vermilion offset contours already fills the frame; by 72.2 to 72.3 it has shrunk to a small burst over the navy fog ground, and it lingers as a small spark glyph until about 73.4 before fading. The previous type block compresses into horizontal lines and disappears around 72.6 to 72.7. A new line appears dim lower-left at 72.8; its first token fills at 73.0, the second at about 73.6 with both filled at 73.6, and by 73.7 the first is neutral bright. A blue halftone container changes from a spiky disc (72.8) to a rotated square (73.0 to 73.5) to a disc (73.7), with its dot screen moving with it. Small ring, plus and dot glyphs appear beside it.
dense_findings.uncertainty: The burst is already full-frame at the first sample, so whether it grew from a point or cut in is unknown; only the shrink-out is observed. The container change could be a morph or a cut sequence. 10 fps sampling.

dense_findings.observation: Not reviewed in this pass; a previous session inspected 20 to 22 s and 24 to 26 s but did not record findings. Whole-video findings for these times come from 2 s overview samples only.
dense_findings.uncertainty: No dense evidence from these windows is used for the design.

assessments.reason: 2D rigid-body physics adds nothing here. Containers, silhouettes and tokens follow authored, lyric-timed transforms, not collisions or stacking.

Selected renderer for the boxed word tokens. Real spans give crisp condensed system-sans text, tight solid vermilion, dim or bright boxes, and a scaled history block. Text stays on solid boxes, clear of dots.

Selected primary renderer. clipPath containers with explicit circles in each shape's local space make the halftone geometry-bound, and transforms move, rotate and scale the screen with its shape. Three-copy offset plates, dashed constellation links and flat grounds are all vector-exact.
Selected motion owner. One paused timeline with a single proxy tween calls a pure render(t), so each property has one owner and direct, backward and repeated seeks match.
It would compete with the GSAP time proxy for the same SVG and token properties. It adds no capability the pure render(t) lacks.

Selected supporting tool, used at build time only. It validates the approximate tokens and checks dim, bright and active-box text contrast on each ground family. It does no interpolation, because tone may only come from dot size.
The style has no data or charts. A chart library would introduce axes the poster language doesn't have.
It only generates basic shapes. The lobed blob, hexagon, star and rotated square are trivial to author as SVG paths, and the Remotion-oriented package adds a dependency for no gain.

Conditional for full video only: it could bake a dense fog or speckle Canvas layer with seeded noise if SVG dot counts get too high. It isn't selected, because it adds a second renderer, rasterises vector print geometry and needs care with redraw determinism.
An Anime.js timeline would be a second clock writing the same attributes as the GSAP proxy. Its line drawing and morphing are covered elsewhere.

Conditional: it could draw constellation link lines or orbit circles on, within the same GSAP timeline. It isn't selected, because the links are static dashed strokes and native stroke-dasharray in render(t) is enough.
Native getTotalLength and getPointAtLength already cover path measurement. Nothing in the style needs partial-path evolution beyond what native SVG does.

Conditional for full video: a cached, seeded Canvas layer for the mottled night fog or paper speckle if SVG node counts exceed budget, with the grid anchored per shape. It isn't the preview default, because it rasterises the flat vector print look.
Its bursts would add an independent effects clock and arbitrary particles. The section-change ink starburst is a single authored path scaled by render(t).

Conditional for full video at very high dot densities: angled round-dot screening with dot size driven by tone suits the style. It needs a grid anchored to each container's object space and masks to protect text, and it risks aliasing and flicker. Not selected for the preview.
Conditional host for a GPU halftone pass if dot fields grow beyond SVG budgets in a long video. For bounded flat poster frames it is unnecessary.

Conditional: a fragment shader could compute shape-bound dot screens and halftone rings from uniforms such as time and the shape's transform. It is the fallback for density, not the default, because of the aliasing risk.
Only conditional, as a flat orthographic host for a ShaderMaterial halftone pass. The style explicitly forbids 3D, so no scene depth, lighting or perspective is used. It isn't selected.
Offline 3D rendering contradicts the flat print-poster medium, and the execution policy disallows it in this environment.
Blender scripting for 3D scenes doesn't fit a flat vector poster, and the execution policy disallows it.
Path-traced 3D lighting contradicts the rule of flat ink and dots with no shading, and it is Blender-bound, which is disallowed.
Conditional supporting host for offline audio timing analysis (librosa) when supplied audio and timing sync are requested, writing a JSON timing map. Not needed for the silent preview.
No raster assets need preparing. Fog, speckle and dots are generated procedurally in the vector or Canvas layers.

An interactive image lightbox, which has no role in a rendered lyric poster video.

Conditional for full video: it could batch very large dot fields as Graphics inside transformed Containers, with the ticker disabled. It isn't selected, because it adds a second renderer and raster output where SVG is sufficient for bounded scenes.

Conditional for full video: it can morph a silhouette between spiky and lobed outlines, or a container between blob, hexagon and star, inside the same GSAP timeline. All three offset copies share the morphed path. Not needed for the 3-second preview, which can cut between path variants.

styles.implementation:
Visual layer (SVG): one inline SVG whose viewBox matches the project-supplied resolution. Each section shows one ground family: night_navy with night_fog cloud fog made of halftone dots, paper_cream with sparse grey speckle, or ray_maroon/ray_black radial rays from an off-centre vanishing point, or concentric halftone rings. Each geometric container (lobed blob, hexagon, rotated square, star, disc) is a <g> whose translate, rotate and scale come from render(t). Inside the group sit a clipPath of the container's own path and dots generated once as explicit circles in local coordinates on a rotated grid. Dot radius is maxR × tone(localPos), using radial or linear tone ramps in halftone_blue or ochre, so the screen travels, rotates and scales with its shape. There are no smooth gradients and no frame-wide overlay. Each hero silhouette is a single path drawn three times: muted_vermilion and cream copies offset 3–8 px in different directions, with the ink_black copy on top. Offsets may drift only as a pure function of t. Outline changes cut between authored spiky and lobed path variants. Fog, speckle, the constellation glyphs (rings, crosses, triangles, sparks, dots) and their thin dashed links come from a seeded mulberry32 PRNG computed once at load, and are placed in negative space away from the type.

Text layer (HTML/CSS): absolutely positioned real <span> word tokens in a heavy condensed system-sans stack. Box geometry is measured deterministically from character counts and font size after fonts are ready. render(t) sets the state: upcoming tokens dim_token with no fill, the current token on a solid muted_vermilion box with neutral_bright text, completed tokens neutral_bright. Hand-overs overlap briefly. A completed line scales down and moves into a single history block in the opposite corner, keeps its last fill briefly, then settles. crimson_alt is the active fill only for an aside line. There are no dots under letterforms.

Motion (GSAP): one paused timeline whose only tween drives proxy.t across the project-supplied duration. Its onUpdate calls a pure render(t) that clamps t and sets every attribute, class and visibility, with no carried state, so forward, backward, repeated and direct seeks are identical. Section changes: the ink starburst and its offset plates cover the frame for a few frames, the ground swaps underneath, then the burst shrinks into a constellation glyph and fades. The outgoing line compresses horizontally and fades before the incoming line appears, so two main lines are never readable at once.

Supporting (chroma.js, build time only): validate the approximate hex tokens and check text contrast for dim, bright and active-box tokens on every ground family. Never interpolate colours.

Preview scope (3 s, silent): one navy section with one hero silhouette, two screened containers and a constellation, then a cut to a maroon-ray chorus beat. The active box steps through the exact supplied copy on an even authored schedule fitted to the supplied duration, with a settled reading hold.

Full video: sections follow the copy and lyric structure. Exact copy, dimensions, duration and audio all come from the project. Token timing uses an offline timing map only when supplied audio and timing analysis are requested; otherwise it uses the authored schedule. Optional MorphSVG transitions for silhouettes and containers, within the same GSAP timeline. Optional cached Canvas 2D or GLSL halftone only if dot counts exceed SVG budgets, with the grid still anchored to each shape.
styles.rationale:
The style is a flat offset-print poster whose defining trait is halftone bound to geometry, plus misregistered vector plates and boxed word tokens. SVG clipPath groups holding explicit local-space dots bind each screen to its shape exactly and stay crisp at any resolution. HTML spans give real, high-contrast text with solid boxes. A single GSAP time proxy feeding a pure render(t) gives one owner per property and safe seeking. chroma.js only verifies contrast; it never recolours.

Alternatives and tradeoffs:
- Canvas 2D, p5.js and PixiJS could batch dense fog and speckle cheaply, but they rasterise the vector print look and add a second renderer, so they stay conditional for full-video density.
- A luminance-based GLSL/WebGL halftone (optionally hosted on a flat Three.js quad) scales to huge dot fields. It needs a grid anchored to each object and text masks, and risks aliasing and flicker, so it is a conditional fallback with no 3D.
- MorphSVG, Paper.js (offline silhouette variants) and DrawSVG are useful for full-video morphs or line draw-ons, but unnecessary in the preview.
- librosa (on a Python host) is used only when supplied audio sync is requested.
- Anime.js, Motion and mo.js would compete with GSAP for the same properties.
- Scrambled text breaks the exact-copy token relay.
- 3D, PBR, toon, bloom, sketch, painterly, photographic and frame-sequence tools contradict the flat ink-and-dot medium, and the Blender-based tools are also disallowed.

Palette roles are preserved: one ground family per section, vermilion only for the active box, offset plates and tiny accents, and tone only through dot size. Hex values are approximate readings, not measured colours.

variables.subject: a small idea growing into a clear, confident voice
variables.audience_and_objective: a general audience; a short style study showing the look in three seconds
variables.assets_and_exact_copy: Two lines, in this order: 'A SMALL IDEA' then 'FINDS ITS VOICE'. No other copy and no image assets.
variables.audio_or_rhythm_requirements: Silent; no audio. Use an authored even word schedule.
variables.render_pipeline: After index.html is written in this workspace: run node node_modules/hyperframes/bin/hyperframes.mjs with its render command at verbose logging on this composition (read only that command's --help for exact flags) to produce rendered/preview.mp4 at 1280x720, 30 fps, 3 seconds, piping all stdout and stderr to logs/render.log. Then load index.html in the headless browser available through the installed hyperframes dependencies, call window.exportPoster(2.4) and write the returned string to rendered/poster.svg, logging to logs/poster.log. Then decode frames at 0.3, 1.0, 1.7, 2.4 and 2.95 seconds from rendered/preview.mp4 into rendered/samples/ as PNG with the ffmpeg used by hyperframes, logging to logs/samples.log. Report the exit status of each step.

variables.subject: an idea becoming a signal
variables.visual_style: Flat print-poster typography on night navy #1a2350, warm cream #f3eee2 completed text, muted grey #7d7a78 upcoming text, muted vermilion #e2552a active word boxes, with sparse stationary halftone accents kept outside all text. No source lyrics, logos or extra copy.
variables.render_pipeline: HyperFrames with local GSAP as the paused composition clock; local esbuild is available through node_modules. Render capture is handled separately after authoring.

visual_verification.editor_inspection: Eight decoded video frames per preview inspected for type readability, token handoff/history, geometry-bound dots, plate offsets and palette roles. This is not a claim of source audio sync or full-speed source playback.

seek.comparison: Decoded RGB pixels after browser paint readiness; direct vs reverse event seeks

software_seek.captureMode: software rasterization, verification only; project renderer unchanged

style.limitation: All eight DOM states match. Some anti-aliased raster samples differ by at most 1/255 in a colour channel (up to 2982 of 921600 pixels), including under software capture; no text, position or section-state drift observed. This is recorded rather than claimed as bit-identical rendering.

observations: Night section has frame-wide two-scale navy cloud mottle, speckle and grain; no flat ground.
Small vermilion/ochre/cobalt cutouts in dashed strings, off-centre, density rising into the chorus.
Warm section uses amber/ochre rays with rust ring screens and a coral dot field.
Screened cream containers (lobed blob, star) with varying dot radius and offset vermilion plate.
Verse copy is a small multi-word lower-left boxed relay; chorus copy is stacked caps top-left with vermilion active box.
No empty or solid black frame; no giant ink hero.
limitations: Cream/cobalt appears only as a diagonal wipe, not a held paper (B) field; the prompt requires B or C so this complies, but the light-paper family is under-represented.
Chorus sets the three-word line FINDS / ITS / VOICE one word per line, against the prompt's no-one-word-per-line rule; judged minor at about 6 percent height, not a reason to redraw.
No ink starburst accent and no history block were used (both optional).
Three-second study cannot show all three ground families; comparison is to sampled stills only.
